entries.proposition: Group size was two animals per sex per group, cynomolgus monkeys, single cisterna magna dose.
The control vector was designed to transduce as efficiently as the expressing vector without producing mRNA from either strand.
entries.snippet: This was designed to transduce cells as efficiently as AAV9.hCLN2 without producing mRNA from either DNA strand of the vector genome

entries.proposition: The in-vitro check of the Null vector in human neurons found an average of 25 RPE65-mapping reads per sample, called negligible by the authors.
entries.snippet: an average of 25 reads mapping to human RPE65 was detected per sample
entries.anchor: Materials and methods, Test article, para 3

entries.proposition: Null vector DNA in brain, cord and DRG was at levels similar to or greater than with the expressing vector.
entries.snippet: at similar or greater levels than those seen with AAV9.hCLN2-treated cynomolgus monkeys

entries.proposition: The authors report no DRG toxicity or other treatment-related finding with the Null vector.
entries.snippet: there was no evidence of DRG toxicity or any other treatment-related findings in these AAV9.Null-treated animals

entries.proposition: The results section records slightly more increased cellularity in lumbosacral DRG with the Null vector (two of four) than with vehicle (one of four) and minimal-to-mild sciatic degeneration, in different animals.
entries.snippet: a higher incidence of increased cellularity (two of four animals) in the DRG (LS only)

entries.proposition: Figure 2: lumbosacral DRG neuronal degeneration scores about 1 to 2 in all expressing-vector groups and zero for the Null group in every region; cervical and thoracic DRG degeneration only at the 1.1e14 dose; lumbosacral nerve-root degeneration about 3 to 4 in expressing groups.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 2 rows cervical, thoracic, lumbar, lumbosacral by columns DRG neuronal degeneration, spinal nerve root degeneration, spinal cord dorsal-tract degeneration: AAV9.Null (open circles) scores 0 in every panel; expressing-vector groups score about 1 to 2 for lumbosacral DRG; the 1.1e14 group (diamonds) alone scores above 0 in cervical, thoracic and lumbar DRG; lumbosacral nerve-root scores about 3 to 4.

entries.proposition: Three purification routes with 74, 86 and 96 percent full capsids all gave the lesion; the authors conclude purification and empty-capsid fraction are not major determinants.
entries.snippet: indicating that the purification process and relative amount of empty capsid are not major determinants of the DRG toxicity

entries.proposition: No effect on sensory or motor nerve conduction in animals with histological change.
entries.snippet: no effects were seen in the neuro-electrophysiological endpoints

entries.proposition: Intraepidermal nerve fibre density fell below the control range in some animals with no dose relationship.
entries.snippet: Thus, the reduction in nerve fiber density was considered to be likely test-article-related in some animals but showed no relationship to dose.

entries.proposition: Figure 4: in the low-dose groups some animals fall from the pre-dose range to about 25 to 30 fibres per mm; the 1.1e14 group shows no fall; group means overlap the control band.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 4 scatter, pre-dose versus week 4 per group: AEX 3.1e13, CEX 3.1e13 and UC 3.1e13 groups show some week-4 values near 25 to 45 fibres per mm; the 1.1e14 AEX group is about 40 to 50 at both times; Null and control near unchanged; grey band is the pre-treatment range.

entries.proposition: MRI was done only in the 1.1e14 hCLN2 group and controls.
The authors conclude DRG toxicity after intrathecal AAV9 is primarily mediated by transgene overexpression, on this study alongside other published data.
entries.snippet: supports a hypothesis that the DRG toxicity in NHPs following intrathecal administration of rAAV9 is primarily mediated by transgene overexpression

entries.proposition: The authors write that in earlier NHP studies immune suppression ablated T-cell responses but not DRG pathology.
entries.snippet: immune suppression ablated T cell responses, but not DRG pathology

entries.proposition: The brain findings unique to this transgene are attributed possibly to an immune response to human TPP1.
entries.snippet: the findings in the brain were possibly an immune-mediated response to the human TPP1

entries.proposition: The authors say the lesions are sub-clinical and that long-term NHP studies suggest they resolve; longer duration was not tested here.
entries.snippet: It is unclear whether or not these changes would have been more apparent in a study of a longer duration.

entries.proposition: The authors say the Null genome lacked a functional promoter, unlike a CAG-promoter no-protein control that did cause cord degeneration after parenchymal injection in an earlier study.
entries.snippet: which lacked a functional promoter and does not produce mRNA or protein
